summary:
## Mastering the DeLonghi Dedica EC685

This guide provides tips for getting the most out of the affordable DeLonghi Dedica home espresso machine, from basic operation to advanced upgrades.

### The Advanced Barista Routine

To move beyond pre-ground coffee and achieve cafe-quality results, you will need a few key items and techniques:

- **Key Tools**: A digital **scale**, a quality **burr grinder** (hand or electric), and fresh, **specialty coffee beans**.
- **Dosing**: Use a scale for precision. The stock portafilter fits about **11 grams**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> After tamping, the coffee puck should not touch the group head when the portafilter is locked in. If it leaves an imprint, you are using too much coffee and must reduce the dose.

- **Grinding**: Espresso requires a **very fine grind**. If your coffee flows too quickly (<20 seconds), your grind is likely too coarse, leading to a sour, under-extracted shot.
- **Preparation**: 
  1. **Preheat** the machine, portafilter, and cup by running hot water through them. This is crucial for lighter roasts.
  2. **Dry** the portafilter basket thoroughly before adding ground coffee.
  3. **Distribute** the coffee grounds evenly in the basket.
  4. **Tamp** with firm, level, medium pressure.

### Example Espresso Recipe

- **Dose**: 11g of coffee
- **Yield**: 30g of liquid espresso
- **Time**: ~25 seconds

### Key Upgrades for Better Coffee

While the stock Dedica is capable, two main upgrades can significantly elevate your coffee experience.

#### Upgrade 1: Non-Pressurized Portafilter

The stock **pressurized portafilter** is forgiving for beginners but limits extraction quality. 

- **Benefit**: Upgrading to a **bottomless, non-pressurized portafilter** allows for a more even extraction, larger doses (e.g., **16.5 grams**), and lets you diagnose issues like channeling. 
- **Result**: More sweetness, complexity, and better body in your espresso.

> [!TIP]
> Pairing a non-pressurized portafilter with a good grinder is the most impactful upgrade for espresso quality.

#### Upgrade 2: Enhanced Milk Steaming

For better latte art and microfoam, you can modify the steam wand.

- **Option A (Free Mod)**: Simply pull off the outer **metal sleeve** from the stock steam wand. This gives you more control, exposing the plastic jet underneath, but it requires more practice to get silky foam.
- **Option B (Paid Upgrade)**: For more power and control, you can purchase and install a **Rancilio steam wand**, a popular modification for this machine.

### Final Takeaways

- The DeLonghi Dedica is an excellent, affordable machine for learning the fundamentals of manual espresso.
- Its main limitations are lower power and temperature stability, which can be a challenge for very light roasted coffees.
- The most significant improvements come from investing in a **good grinder** and upgrading to a **non-pressurized portafilter**.
transcription:
## Introduction to Better Home Espresso

In this video, we want to share the tips on making the best possible coffee using a cheap home espresso machine like this one. We picked DeLonghi Dedica as it is a very affordable espresso machine you can get at around 150 Euros. If you have it already or plan on buying it, we will share some tips and tricks to make the best possible coffee out of it.

## DeLonghi Dedica: Features and Requirements

When you look at the Dedica, it's a small and frankly quite pretty espresso machine that fits nicely on most kitchen counters. It has a water tank that fits around one liter of water, a portafilter with a pressurized filter basket, three control buttons, a steam wand with a hot water dispenser, and a switch on/off control.

Unlike automatic espresso machines, two things make using it a little more complicated but also more fun. First, you need to have an external grinder, which is essential to brewing tasty coffee, yet it adds to the budget, or you will depend on pre-ground coffee. Second, it's quite simple to use it, but there are more steps than just pressing a button. You need to dose the coffee, put it into a portafilter, tamp it, and control the dose. You need to learn some basic barista skills.

## Basic vs. Advanced Routines

Okay, so let's make coffee now. We will start with a simple routine with pre-ground coffee, and then we will progress towards a more sophisticated barista routine that yields nice tasting espresso using specialty coffee beans.

## Advanced Tools & Dosing Theory

So this was a super simple method how to make espresso with pre-ground coffee. But now we will show you a more advanced technique. We will need a scale to weigh our coffee and coffee beverage, whole bean specialty coffee to get a better experience, and a high-quality hand grinder.

So now we pre-weighed 11.5 grams of coffee. In espresso grinding, which is very fine, sometimes the coffee gets stuck on the grinder, so I'm going to use 11 grams for proving the espresso. Why 11 grams? Every portafilter has a different size. When you grind the coffee, tamp it in the portafilter, and put it inside the machine; if you lock it, the coffee shouldn't be touching the group head. So after you do this, when you take out the portafilter, the coffee ground should be dry and clean and shouldn't be broken or shouldn't be wet from the group head. If it's touching the group head, this should never happen, and you need to decrease the amount of the coffee.

## Grinding and Preheating

Let's grind our coffee. I'm using a hand grinder which is a very high quality grinder that you can use for espresso, but you can also use different grinders or electric grinders. The important thing is that the grinder is able to grind very fine for the espresso preparation. If the grinder cannot grind fine for espresso, you end up with the coffee that's flowing too quickly and it will become under-extracted, watery, and sour. So let's grind.

Nice, the coffee is ground. One more thing we will do: we are using a specialty coffee that is roasted for espresso, but still it's a much lighter roast than pre-ground or very dark roasted coffee. For brewing and achieving higher extraction and better taste, we need to preheat the machine so it's as hot as possible. So first we'll just rinse it with hot water.

Okay, now the portafilter is wet and if you will put the coffee inside, it would start preparing, it would touch the water and the extraction would start. So we need to dry it nice and clean.

## Precision Dosing, Leveling, and Tamping

We'll put the portafilter on the scale. This is a little guy who will help us to get all the coffee inside the portafilter and not everywhere around. Now I tare the scale just to check our 11 grams. Put the coffee inside. And we have a little bit more, so I'll just take a bit. There we go, 11 grams. 

Why is it important to know how much coffee you use? Because if you want to change something while brewing and the coffee flows very quickly or slowly, sometimes it can be that you use more and less grams. Because this measurement is the volume measurement, but the different coffee you use or a different grind this coffee is, you will always have different amount of the grounds. So once you can wait, seven grams will be full. The second time it will be the same but it will weigh 8 grams. So the more precise measurement is using a scale. That's where you always have the same amount of the coffee, and if you need to change the brewing time, you will adjust the grinder.

So we'll level up the coffee. Try to have the same amount of the coffee everywhere, so when we tamp it, we have the same extraction on every point of the coffee bed.

I use this tamper, but of course you can probably find on the internet something nicer. This is a bit clumsy, but it works. So just insert, straight, level up, and then medium pressure press the beans. You don't need to use so much pressure, just like medium pressure. Take it out. Clean. So let's try.

## Pulling the Shot and Tasting

As you could notice, straight after I inserted the portafilter, I pressed the button. It's the best practice to start brewing as soon as possible. In the beginning, the coffee is flowing very slowly. Maybe it takes a few seconds after it starts dripping. That's all right. And the whole extraction time will be around 25 seconds.

So there is our espresso. Using 11 grams of freshly ground specialty coffee, we have 30 grams of the beverage in the cup and the extraction time was 25 seconds. Nothing else than to taste it. Smells quite fruity and cherry-like. Okay. It's quite surprisingly sweet. There is a little bit higher acidity maybe, but that's still drinkable. It has cherry notes, chocolate notes. The body is somewhere between espresso and lungo. Quite pleasant, and definitely better than pre-ground coffee.

## Making a Cappuccino: The Base

Now we're going to make cappuccino, making the same espresso, only this time we use a larger cup.

So let's make a cappuccino now. The espresso is ready. Here is our fresh whole-fat milk. You need the whole-fat milk to make a microfoam, to have enough proteins and fat. It's good to use the amount you will need for the cappuccino, not more and not too little, because then the foam will stand in the end and you will have foam everywhere. So a bit more milk than you need into the cup.

Before we start steaming the milk, we have to switch on the steam button. Without it, we will have hot water coming out of the steam wand. So we switch it on, wait a couple of seconds. And now before we start, we will release the hot water that's condensated inside the steam wand. So just by starting the handle for a little bit, we release the hot water, switch it off. And now we'll use only dry air to steam the milk.

## Steaming Milk with the Stock Wand

Of course it takes a bit longer because this machine doesn't have such power like professional machines. That's also why we don't steam the milk while we brew espresso. First we do espresso, then we steam the milk. 

So here is our foam. It's not difficult to make it. Actually, it's easier, and you have to be careful not to overdo it and get too much foam, which we have now a bit more for the latte art, but we will make it work. Okay, let's see what we can do because we have a bit more foam than we would need, but...

Okay. I'm not a cappuccino guy, but this tastes pretty nice. It has nice creamy texture. There is a bit more foam. It's a bit more foamy than it should be, but I think it's pretty enjoyable and I would love having this at home or at someone's visit.

## Upgrade 1: Non-Pressurized Portafilter

Now I want to show you a couple of upgrades. First one is concerning the espresso. DeLonghi uses a pressurized portafilter. This allows you for more mistakes in grinding, or if you have a cheaper grinder, it will allow you to make a drinkable espresso. But if you want to take your experience even higher, you can use a portafilter like in a professional cafe, which is not pressurized. This will allow you to extract more flavor and get higher quality from your espresso. So we are going to brew with the bottomless portafilter, and we are going to use 16.5 grams. By using more coffee, we will again should achieve espresso of higher quality. So let's try.

Also you can buy a better tamper that's 51 millimeters in diameter.

This is actually like really, really nice espresso. I'm surprised, honestly. It has better body, more sweetness, more complexity and more layers in the flavors. It's really nice and with a good grinder, it's a no-brainer to get the bottomless portafilter that is non-pressurized to get a much higher quality in your espresso.

## Upgrade 2: Better Milk Steaming

Now let's jump to the second tip that will be focused on the latte art and milk steaming. To get better milk texture which will allow you to make better latte art as well, there are two options. One is you can buy an extra steam wand from Rancilio which costs again around 30 Euros. You need a little bit of technical skills, but it shouldn't be so complicated to take the machine apart and change the steam wall with the Rancilio steam wand. You will get much more control and power into the steaming.

The second option that costs you zero is to just take out the metal part of the steam wand on the DeLonghi and you can use only the plastic one that's attached here. It's much better for steaming, although you need a little bit of the practice, but the result is better microfoam and better latte art. 

This cappuccino has definitely much better texture and much better microfoam. Although it is harder to achieve it when you are not using this metal part, you have to control and put a same amount of the air and you have to do it slowly and with patience to get a better microfoam. But in the end, you will achieve definitely better quality than using this thing. And if you practice enough, you are definitely going to have a better latte art than me, easily.

## Conclusion and Final Thoughts

Overall, Dedica is a definitely great looking home espresso machine. It comes at a very affordable price. You can brew pretty good espressos and learn how to work around the manual espresso machine while practicing basic barista and latte art skills. Of course Dedica has its limits. It will not allow you to extract perfectly light roasted specialty coffees, mainly because of lower power and lower temperature. But still, to improve the performance, there are few upgrades that will help you achieve much better results for both espresso and milk steaming. Thanks for watching, guys. Enjoy your coffee and see you next time.
